+Also fixed: a prop passed explicitly as `undefined` (and not set by `attrs`) is now forwarded to a wrapped component so that component can fall back to its own default, the pattern MUI's `ButtonBase` relies on (for example `<Root role="button" {...props} />`). A DOM tag such as `styled.div` still drops the prop, since browsers have no "undefined" attribute. A component that checks `'role' in props` may see the key where it did not before.
+To let a caller's `undefined` clear an `attrs` default, use the function form and check for the prop:
+`rel={undefined}` then renders no `rel`, and omitting the prop renders `rel="noopener"`.
+Fix TypeScript errors in projects that augment React HTML props with a `data-*` template-literal index signature.

+In development, a console warning now appears when the browser finds server-rendered styles from a different styled-components version than the one running. Those styles were previously skipped without notice, which left class names stale and hydration mismatched. Make sure the server and the browser load the same version (`npm ls styled-components` lists duplicates).

-React Native: passing `prop={undefined}` to a styled component opts out of an `attrs()`-provided default, matching web behavior. `<Comp accessible={undefined} />` renders with no `accessible` prop even when the component has `.attrs({ accessible: true })`.

+Fixed a protocol-relative value after a colon being removed as a `//` line comment. `--cdn: //cdn.example.com/x.png;` now keeps its value, with or without spaces between the colon and the slashes. A `//` on a later line than the colon is still removed as a comment.
+Added a `StyledComponent<Target, Props>` type for annotating explicitly-typed styled component exports.

+Packages that emit their own declaration files, including any project using `isolatedDeclarations`, must annotate every exported styled component, and there was no public type for it: consumers reached into internal paths or hand-assembled one that dropped members like a wrapped component's hoisted statics.
+`StyledComponent` is exported from the web and native entries. Name the target and props as you passed them to `styled`:
+It resolves to the exact type `styled(Target)<Props>` produces, so the annotation is not lossy.
+`styled()` wrapping a generic polymorphic component keeps its declared props narrow.

+Wrapping a component whose props are generic over an element type, such as the common `<C extends React.ElementType>(props: PolymorphicProps<C, OwnProps>)` pattern, let the styled result accept prop values the component itself rejects: `styled(Button)` would take `variant="anything"` even though `<Button variant="anything">` is a type error. The wrapper now narrows those props exactly as the direct component does, so a bad value is caught in both places. Valid props, children, and plain (non-generic) targets are unaffected.

+Fixed errors inside styled-components' own type declarations, with `skipLibCheck` turned off, for projects without `@types/react-dom` or `@types/node` installed. The `ServerStyleSheet` streaming API's types referenced types that only those packages provide. `interleaveWithNodeStream` still accepts the result of `renderToPipeableStream` and Node readable streams exactly as before, and with `@types/node` installed it still returns a full Node stream type.

The test is `'style' extends keyof P`, not `P extends { style?: infer S }`. The latter is vacuously satisfied by `{}`, which hands a `style` key to targets that expose no props at all and defeats `WidenForUntypedTarget`.

+A bag with a string index signature (`string extends keyof P`) passes through unwidened. A generic polymorphic component introspects at its `ElementType` constraint and gains `[k: string]: any`; `Omit` over that index collapses every narrow key into it, so `styled(Button)` would accept props `Button` rejects (#5756).

+Under an app's `data-${string}` template-index augmentation of `React.HTMLAttributes`, `IntrinsicProps` switches to a `FastOmit` variant: distributing `Omit`'s `Exclude` over the template key across every intrinsic element exceeds the union limit (TS2590, #5796). The switch is a global constant, so the unaugmented path keeps built-in `Omit`. An `aria-${string}` augmentation is not detected.

The `& {}` wrap inside `style?: CSSPropertiesWithVars | (P[keyof P & 'style'] & {}) | undefined` is a real undefined-filter under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`; DO NOT remove it. Without it, both `style?:` AND `style: undefined` become assignable, which changes semantics. The explicit `| undefined` then restores `style={undefined}`.
Don't replace built-in `Omit` with `FastOmit` in `WithCSSVars`; built-in `Omit` (Pick + Exclude) is more optimized (+17% instantiations when replaced).

- Negative assertions use `@ts-expect-error` on the line directly above the offending expression, each with a one-line comment stating what must fail. This is a deliberate test, not a suppression: if the type gets looser and the error stops occurring, the directive itself errors as unused, which flags the regression.

- `declare module` augmentation is project-wide: it leaks into every file in the same `tsc` program. The suite augments the declaration's own source location (`'../models/ThemeProvider'` for `DefaultTheme`, `'react'` for `CSSProp`) because the test imports from `src`, not the published package; consumers instead augment the public specifier, `declare module 'styled-components'`. If a future augmentation test needs a variant that would collide with the suite's, give it its own tsconfig project (including only that file) run as a separate `tsc` pass, rather than letting two augmentations collide in one program.
